cert.note.model: Verified by substitution and simplification; no search required.
cert.note.unsat_core: Verifying requires re-solving, but only the core (far smaller).
cert.note.lp_dual.exact: Optimality certified in EXACT rationals: primal and dual feasibility plus c.x = b.y, all in Fraction. No tolerances and no trust in CBC.
cert.note.lp_dual.float: Weak duality in FLOATING POINT, with a tolerance. Fine for exploring; citing a constant needs exact mode.
cert.note.cegis: The list of counterexamples IS the certificate: it is the minimal set of inputs that pins this solution down.
cert.note.cnf_model: Checked clause by clause. No solver, no propagation.
cert.note.drat: Refutation proof. Checked by unit propagation (RUP/RAT): no SAT solver is involved, so the one that produced it need not be trusted.
cert.note.shrink_graph: Minimal (1-minimal), not minimum. `blocked` is the witness: every one-step reduction either fails a filter or satisfies the predicate. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.
cert.note.mus: Minimal unsatisfiable subset. The DRAT proof refutes the MUS and each witness is a model of the MUS without one of its clauses: together they certify unsatisfiability AND minimality without a solver.
cert.note.bisect: The threshold is certified by the pair that brackets it: a proof on the good side and a refutation on the bad side. Each is verified separately. MONOTONICITY in t is assumed, not proved.
cert.note.synth_proved: Two chained obligations: the bounded synthesis that found the candidate and the universal symbolic proof of it. Each is verified separately; the one that counts as a theorem is the second.
cert.note.sweep: Two different things: which family was examined (verifiable here) and whether the predicate was evaluated correctly on each graph (only if the predicate supplied a certificate: {certified} of {total} entries). COMPLETENESS of the family requires re-enumerating.
cert.note.graph_set: Verifies pairwise non-isomorphism and the filters. COMPLETENESS (that none is missing) can only be checked by re-enumerating.
verify.model.fails: the assignment does NOT satisfy the formula
verify.core.detail: core of {n} formulas (includes the negated claim)
verify.lp.exact.detail: EXACT rational arithmetic, no tolerances: optimum = {value}
verify.lp.float.detail: weak duality with a tolerance; to cite it, re-run in exact mode
verify.lp.float.warning: FLOATING-POINT certificate with tolerance 1e-6: not usable to cite an exact constant
verify.cegis.impl_ok: the implementation satisfies its own constraints
verify.drat.formula: the formula matches the declared one ({n} clauses)
verify.drat.steps: the proof is RUP/RAT step by step
verify.drat.detail: {steps} steps ({rup} RUP, {rat} RAT, {del} deletions) in {ms:.0f} ms
verify.sweep.stats: the statistics match the stored values
verify.sweep.detail: family of {n} graphs; does NOT verify completeness (that needs re-enumerating)

verify.sweep.unevaluated: {n} graphs were never evaluated (errors or inconclusive)

Verifiable here: the ids are unique, the statistics match the stored values, and each predicate certificate checks out. NOT verifiable here: that the domain is complete or that the ids denote what they claim -- that is the spec's responsibility.

verify.family.programmable: {names} cannot be re-checked here: a programmable filter lives in the spec

verify.range.nothing_below: nothing failed below the first failure
verify.range.stopped: stopped at the first failure: the larger sizes were NOT examined

The trace records the index taken into reduce() at each step, so verification replays the exact descent instead of re-running the search. `blocked` is the witness that no one-step reduction survives. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.

engine.farkas.found: {mode} certificate found: {n} hypotheses with a non-zero multiplier
engine.farkas.none: no {mode} certificate exists for this system
engine.farkas.not_polynomial: cannot be put in polynomial form: {detail}

cert.note.farkas: Non-negative rational multipliers whose combination cancels every monomial and closes the system. Verified by multiplying and adding in Fraction: no solver, no search. This is what linarith emits; with nonlinear=true the extra rows are products and squares of the hypotheses, which is what nlinarith adds.

cert.note.proof: A proof assembled from lemmas. Each lemma carries its own certificate AND the link showing that what the certificate establishes entails the statement used downstream. Lemmas marked as bridges are verified but not linked: the step from what they establish to a formula is a modelling decision, and it is listed by name so the reader can weigh it.
verify.proof.link: lemma {name}: its certificate entails the statement used
verify.proof.step_link: the final step uses only the lemmas and the theorem's own hypotheses
verify.proof.unused: lemmas the theorem does not need: {names}

verify.ball.no_claim: no claim: the enclosure is the result
verify.ball.reproduced: re-evaluating the spec lands inside it

engine.prove.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses contradict each other, so this goal -- and every other goal -- follows. The proof is valid and says nothing. Run `check` on the hypotheses alone to find which pair clashes.
engine.farkas.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses close the system without the goal at all, so they are contradictory and any goal would have been proved.
verify.core.vacuous: VACUOUS: this core does not include the negated goal, so the hypotheses contradict each other and the proof holds for any goal.
verify.farkas.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses were found to close the system without the goal, so they are contradictory and any goal would follow. The certificate is valid and says nothing.
verify.proof.vacuous: VACUOUS: the lemmas contradict each other, so the theorem -- and any other -- follows from them. Check the lemma statements against each other before citing this.
cli.vacuous: the hypotheses are contradictory: this proof is vacuous

engine.induct.empty_base: the base is empty: k0={k0} is above base_upto={upto}
engine.induct.gap: the chain does not join: the step starts at k={step} but the base only reaches {upto}. Every n between them is proved by nothing
engine.induct.base_missing: base case k={k}: no certificate at {path}
engine.induct.base_invalid: base case k={k}: its certificate does not verify ({detail})
engine.induct.base_failed: base case k={k} was not established [{status}]: {detail}
engine.induct.bad_base: a base case must be a Spec, SweepSpec, DomainSpec, CNFSpec or a certificate path, not a {got}
engine.induct.step_failed: the inductive step was not proved [{status}]: {detail}
engine.induct.step_link: the step was proved, but what its certificate establishes does not entail the step statement
engine.induct.proved: {n} base cases k={k0}..{upto}, step from k={step}, chained by induction
engine.induct.conclusion: the property holds for every n >= {k0}
cert.note.induction: The induction schema, applied: a certificate per base case, a certificate for the step proved with the index FREE, and the two numbers that decide whether the chain joins. The schema itself is not a solver result and does not pretend to be one.
verify.induction.covered: the base cases are exactly k0..base_upto
verify.induction.joins: the step starts no later than the base ends
verify.induction.step_link: the step certificate entails the step statement
verify.induction.bridge: BRIDGE at k={k}: a finite check read as the property -- {why}
verify.induction.schema: The induction over the naturals is APPLIED here, not verified by a solver. It is one fixed schema, unlike a bridge, but it is still a step no certificate in this file performs.
verify.induction.detail: {n} base cases k={k0}..{upto}, plus the step

cli.orbits.by_orbit: evaluated {evaluated} representatives, inferred {inferred}. INVARIANCE ASSUMED, not proved; {n} spot checks agreed.

verify.orbits.spot: the spot checks agree with their representatives
verify.sweep.replay.no_symmetry: the spec no longer declares a symmetry, so the inference cannot be reproduced

verify.witness.same_run: the witnesses minimise the sweep's own representatives

lean.lemma.derived: DERIVED and linked by certo, via `{engine}`. Its certificate entails this statement; what is left is to restate it in your own encoding and prove it.
lean.lemma.bridge: BRIDGE. Nothing proved this in Lean: {why}
lean.check.no_lake: no `lake` on PATH, so nothing compiled this. The file is emitted either way; it has simply not been checked
lean.check.no_project: {path} is not a Lean project (no lakefile), so `lake env lean` has no Mathlib to import. Emit into a project, or pass --lean-project

poly.budget.pairs: Buchberger gave up after {n} S-pairs: this ideal is too big for an exact computation here. Raise the budget, or reduce the number of variables
poly.budget.terms: a polynomial grew past {n} terms during the Groebner computation
numbers.not_prime: {n} is not prime, so there is no primality certificate for it
numbers.too_deep: the Pratt recursion went too deep at {n}
verify.pratt.complete: the factor list is all of {n}-1
verify.pratt.order: and no smaller order: {n} is prime
sos.no_numpy: numpy is not installed, so there is nothing to search for a Gram matrix with
sos.odd_degree: the polynomial has odd degree {d}, so it takes negative values and cannot be a sum of squares
sos.no_rounding: a numeric Gram matrix was found, but none of the {n} roundings survived exact re-verification. The search landed too close to the boundary of the PSD cone
cert.note.ideal: Cofactors h_i with f = sum h_i g_i. Finding them is a Groebner basis computation; checking them is expanding a product and comparing coefficients, in exact rationals. With f = 1 the system has no common solution over the complex numbers, hence over the reals, the rationals and the integers.
cert.note.sos: p = sum d_i q_i^2 with rational d_i and rational linear forms q_i. The Gram matrix was found in floating point and is not here -- it was the search. Checking this is multiplying polynomials.
cert.note.number: A Pratt primality tree: a witness generating (Z/n)^*, and a certificate for each prime factor of n-1, recursively down to 2. Checking it is modular exponentiation and nothing else.
verify.ideal.expands: the combination expands to the claim
verify.ideal.member: the claim vanishes on every common root
verify.ideal.field: This refutes solutions over the COMPLEX numbers, hence over the reals, rationals and integers too. The converse does not follow: had no certificate been found, a real solution would still not be implied.
verify.sos.expands: the squares add up to the polynomial
verify.sos.detail: a sum of {n} squares, in exact rationals
engine.ideal.inconsistent: the system has NO common solution: 1 is in the ideal, and the cofactors prove it
engine.ideal.member: the claim vanishes on every common root of the system, certified by {n} cofactors
engine.ideal.not_member: the claim does NOT follow from the equations: it is not in the ideal they generate. That is conclusive, not a timeout
engine.ideal.consistent: the system may have a solution: 1 is not in the ideal, so there is a common root over the complex numbers. Nothing here says whether a REAL one exists
engine.sos.found: a sum of {n} squares, exact, with denominator {denom}
engine.sos.none: no exact sum-of-squares certificate found. NOT a refutation: from degree 4 in 3 variables there are non-negative polynomials that are not sums of squares. {detail}
engine.number.prime: {n} is prime, with a Pratt certificate of {checks} modular checks
engine.number.composite: {n} is NOT prime, so there is no primality certificate: {detail}
engine.number.factored: {n} = {factors}, every factor with its own primality certificate
engine.opt.ilp_tight: integer optimum {value}, CERTIFIED: a feasible integral point achieves it and the exact dual bounds it there
engine.opt.ilp_gap: best integral point found: {value}. The exact dual bounds the optimum by {bound}, so the true optimum lies between them -- CBC's answer is not certified to be optimal
engine.opt.ilp_bound_only: no feasible integral point survived the exact check; all that is certified is the relaxation bound {bound}
verify.lp.ilp_bound: This is an ILP and no integral point travelled with it, so what is certified is the RELAXATION bound, not the integer optimum.
verify.lp.ilp_gap: The integral point achieves {value} and the dual bounds the optimum by {bound}. They differ, so the integer optimum is somewhere between and is NOT certified by this.
spec.bad_kind: {kind} is not a variable kind; known: {known}
engine.mixed.no_discrete: no discrete variables: declare some with kind='binary' or kind='integer', or use `opt`
engine.mixed.out_of_bounds: the search returned {var} outside its declared bounds once rounded
engine.mixed.residual_failed: the discrete choice leaves an infeasible continuous problem: {detail}
engine.mixed.inexact: the residual LP did not certify exactly, so nothing here would be citable
engine.mixed.infeasible: the rounded design violates {name} (and {n} constraints in total). The search's answer did not survive being checked exactly
engine.mixed.short: certified design reaching {value}, SHORT of the target {target} by {deficit}
engine.mixed.design: certified design reaching {value}; the relaxation bounds any design by {bound}
engine.mixed.optimal: certified design reaching {value}, which MEETS the relaxation bound: this is the global optimum
cert.note.mixed_design: A discrete skeleton, the exact continuous packing inside it, and what the two attain. Certified: the assignment is integral and in range, the full point satisfies every original constraint exactly, the residual LP is that problem with this assignment substituted, and its dual is exact. NOT certified, unless the achieved value meets the relaxation bound: that this skeleton is the best one.
verify.mixed.integral: the discrete assignment really is discrete
verify.mixed.feasible: the full point satisfies every original constraint
verify.mixed.value: it attains the value it claims
verify.mixed.residual: the residual LP's own certificate holds

cert.note.gap: The integrality gap of a packing, with both sides attached: the fractional optimum with its exact dual and the integral one with a feasible point. Verification checks the two halves are about the SAME packing, which two files in a folder cannot say. `tight` names the resources carrying positive load -- the obstruction, in the language of the problem.

cert.note.farkas_ray: A Farkas ray: y >= 0 with A^T y >= 0 and b.y < 0, which makes Ax <= b, x >= 0 unsolvable. Checking it is three dot products in exact rationals -- no solver, and no trusting the one that said infeasible.
cert.note.branch_bound: The optimum, and the account of every design not taken. Each node is closed by a certificate -- an exact dual bounding its subtree below the incumbent, a Farkas ray showing it is empty, or the residual LP of a fully fixed design -- and the tree is checked to COVER the integer domain node by node. A tree with a missing child reads exactly like a complete one.

engine.peak.not_shown: NOT ESTABLISHED for {floor}: the step test A <= q'(x*) <= -A could not be shown on the ray, with q'(x*) = {slope}. That says the route failed, not that a better integer exists
cert.note.integer_peak: no integer beats the claimed maximiser, and the maximiser attains the value: a whole family at once
verify.peak.concave: the quadratic is concave on the whole ray
verify.peak.integral: the maximiser is an integer at every integer parameter
verify.peak.step: no integer step improves it: A <= q'(x*) <= -A
verify.peak.value: the value is the objective at the maximiser, expanded
verify.peak.method: checked by expanding polynomials and reading signs, no solver
verify.peak.detail: the integer maximum is {value}, attained at {argmax}, for all {floor}
verify.peak.scope: this is the maximum over the INTEGER variable, for every parameter value at or above the floor. It says nothing below it, and the parameters themselves are assumed integral -- that is what makes the maximiser one.
commands.q.peak: I solved it for n = 1..40. Which integer is best for EVERY n?
cli.peak.scope: and that is every integer choice with {floor} -- not a sample of them
verify.bb.tied: each node's dual is checked against that node's OWN problem, derived from the root
verify.bb.derived: {n} closed nodes, each rebuilt from the root system
verify.bb.untied: this certificate predates the root system being carried, so each node's certificate was checked on its own terms and NOTHING ties it to that node's subproblem. A certificate belonging to a different node would pass. Re-run the search to get one that is tied.
orbits.both: declare `canonicalize` or `labelling`, not both: one asks to be believed and the other asks to be checked, and running both would leave it unclear which one the orbits came from
orbits.no_relabel: a supplied labelling needs an item that can be relabelled -- an `n` and a `relabelled(perm)` -- and {got} has neither
orbits.not_a_permutation: the labelling is not a permutation of the {n} ground points ({got} entries given): a map that is not a bijection renames the object into a different one rather than the same one
verify.orbits.all_witnessed: every member of every orbit carries its permutation
verify.orbits.witnessed: each member IS the representative relabelled, by re-applying the stored permutation
verify.orbits.reapplied: {n} re-applied, {skipped} carried but not decodable, failing: {names}
verify.orbits.one_way: what the witnesses show is that members of an orbit are the SAME object relabelled. They do not show that two different representatives are different objects -- that needs the labelling to be isomorphism-invariant, which is the part certo did not compute and cannot check.
exists.empty_universe: the universe is empty: there is nothing to cover, so the question has no content
exists.foreign: {n} candidate parts cover elements outside the universe ({names}): a part that reaches outside is not a part of this problem
exists.negative_cap: a cap of {k} parts is not a question anything can answer
engine.exists.no_candidates: say what the cover may be built FROM: `candidates` (or `parts`). Without it there is nothing to search over, and assuming every subset would answer a question nobody asked
engine.exists.found: a cover EXISTS: {n} parts chosen from {total} candidates, and it is certified by counting rather than by the solver that found it
engine.exists.none: NO exact cover exists over these {n} candidate parts, for a universe of {universe}. The DRAT refutation says so; it needs no solver to re-check
engine.exists.none_atleast: NO cover exists over these {n} candidate parts, for a universe of {universe}. The DRAT refutation says so; it needs no solver to re-check
commands.q.exists: Does one exist at all -- and if not, can you prove it?
cli.exists.scope: this says no cover exists USING THESE CANDIDATES. That is the same as 'none exists' exactly when the candidates are every part that could have been used, which is a fact about the spec
drup.bad_step: step {k} is neither RUP nor RAT: {lits}
drup.no_empty: the proof does not derive the empty clause
family.max_only: every item program must be a maximisation, and this one says sense={sense}. Bounding a minimum from above needs a primal point, not a dual, which is a different certificate
family.empty: the family is empty: the maximum of nothing is not a number
family.duplicate_ids: {n} items share an id, so a bound stored for one would be read as a bound for the other. Give `key` something that tells them apart
family.inexact: {n} item programs could not be solved EXACTLY ({names}). A float optimum is not a bound, and a family maximum built on one would be a number nobody checked
cert.note.family_extremum: the winner attains the value; every other item is bounded by it. Needs the spec to re-derive the programs
verify.family_max.ids: the item ids match the family they were recorded over
verify.family_max.every_item: every item in the family is accounted for
verify.family_max.counts: {n} of {total} items carry the winner or a bound
verify.family_max.attained: the winner ATTAINS the value: an exact primal and dual that meet
verify.family_max.bounded: every other item is bounded by it, by weak duality
verify.family_max.no_spec: the item programs are NOT stored, so without the spec the vectors here are numbers about nothing and NOTHING was checked ({reason})
verify.family_max.unverified: claims a maximum of {value}, and none of it could be checked
verify.family_max.method: by rebuilding each item's program from the spec and re-checking its vector
verify.family_max.detail: the maximum over {n} items is {value}, attained at {argmax}
verify.family_max.scope: this is the maximum over the family the SPEC defines. It does not verify that the family is the one you meant -- completeness of `items` is the spec's claim, the way a sweep's domain is.
commands.q.family: What is the largest of these ten thousand LPs -- and can nothing beat it?
engine.family.proved: the maximum over {n} items is {value}, attained at {argmax}
ratio.pair: a side is a polynomial, a number, or a (numerator, denominator) pair; this one has {n} entries
ratio.not_poly: a side must be a Poly, a number, or a (numerator, denominator) pair, not {got}
ratio.wrong_ring: this lives in ({got}) and the parameters are ({want})
ratio.relation: the relation must be `<=` or `<`, and this says `{rel}`. `>=` is the same claim with the sides swapped, and two spellings of one statement is how a sign error hides
engine.ratio.denominator: NOT ESTABLISHED: a denominator could not be shown positive on the ray ({which}). Clearing it preserves the direction only when it is positive, and a negative one would flip the inequality -- so this is refused rather than assumed
engine.ratio.not_shown: NOT ESTABLISHED for {floor}: {difference} could not be shown non-negative on the ray. The shift test is sufficient and not necessary, so this says the route failed, not that the inequality is false
cert.note.ratio_bound: denominators cleared after being shown positive, then the difference signed on the ray
verify.ratio.denominators: both denominators are positive on the whole ray
verify.ratio.expanded: the difference is the two sides cross-multiplied, expanded
verify.ratio.sign: the difference is non-negative on the whole ray
verify.ratio.sign_strict: the difference is strictly positive on the whole ray
verify.ratio.method: checked by cross-multiplying, expanding, and reading signs -- no solver
verify.ratio.scope: this holds for every parameter value at or above the floor ({floor}) and says nothing below it.
commands.q.ratio: Is this fraction inequality true for EVERY n, without a solver?
verify.ratio.relation: the relation is one this verifier understands
moment.not_rational: {where} is not an exact rational: {got}. A probability arriving as a float is the failure this command exists to stop
moment.one_shape: give `events` or `tails`, not both and not neither: one is a sum of probabilities and the other is a distribution, and running both would leave it unclear which produced the expectation
moment.relation: the relation must be `<` or `<=`, and this says `{rel}`
engine.moment.exists: E[X] = {value} {rel} {threshold}, so SOME OUTCOME HAS NONE of them: an object avoiding every one of these {n} events exists
engine.moment.fails: E[X] = {value}, which is NOT {rel} {threshold}. That is the arithmetic, not a failed route
engine.moment.range: {n} values are not probabilities ({names}): a negative mass or one above one is not a distribution
cert.note.first_moment: an exact sum of rationals, and the existence a mean below one buys
verify.moment.masses: the masses are the successive tail differences, and none is negative
verify.moment.expectation: the expectation is the sum of the terms, re-added
verify.moment.relation: the relation is one this verifier understands
verify.moment.comparison: the comparison holds, in exact rationals
verify.moment.conclusion: the existence conclusion is drawn exactly when it is earned
verify.moment.earned: a count, a mean strictly below one: some outcome has none
verify.moment.bound_only: a bound on a mean, and nothing is claimed to exist
verify.moment.method: by re-adding exact rationals and comparing, no solver
verify.moment.detail_exists: E[X] = {value} {rel} {threshold}, so an outcome with none of them EXISTS
verify.moment.scope: the probabilities are the spec's claim. What is checked is that they are probabilities, that the sum is the sum, and that the comparison holds -- not that they describe the experiment you meant.
verify.moment.not_a_count: the quantity is NOT declared a count, so no existence follows: a mean below one for something that could be one half everywhere puts no outcome at zero.
commands.q.moment: Is the expected number of bad events below one -- so one good object exists?
entry.empty: the sequence is empty, so there is no index to be the first one
entry.direction: `direction` must be "up" or "down", and this says {got}
entry.negative_step: a step bound of {delta} is not a bound on anything
engine.entry.proved: first crosses {threshold} at index {index}, where the value is {value}
engine.entry.window: first crosses {threshold} at index {index}, where the value is {value} -- and by at most the step bound, so inside [{threshold}, {window})
engine.entry.never: the sequence never crosses {threshold} in its {n} values. That is the sequence, not a failed route -- there is no first index because there is no crossing
engine.entry.steps: the declared step bound {delta} does not hold on the way to the crossing, so the window it would buy is not there. A bound that fails earlier is a bound somebody got wrong
cert.note.first_entry: it crosses here, it had not crossed before, and a step bound says by how little
verify.entry.crosses: the sequence crosses at the claimed index
verify.entry.earliest: it had NOT crossed at any earlier index
verify.entry.indexed: the index is the end of the stored prefix
verify.entry.steps: every step of the prefix respects the declared bound
verify.entry.window: the window is the threshold plus one step
verify.entry.method: by re-finding the crossing in exact rationals, no solver
verify.entry.detail: first crosses at index {index}, where the value is {value}
verify.entry.detail_window: first crosses at index {index}, value {value}, inside [{threshold}, {window})
verify.entry.scope: the prefix carries {n} values and nothing past the crossing, because nothing past it is part of the claim. That the sequence is the one you meant is the spec's claim.
commands.q.entry: Where does this first cross the line -- and by how little?
cli.ask.unknown: nothing here runs a {got}. `certo commands` lists which command answers which question
cli.ask.needs_flags: a {got} goes to `certo {command}`, which needs a decision this cannot make for you -- run it directly and say which mode you want
commands.q.ask: I wrote the spec. Just run whatever answers it.
cli.lean.hollow: {n} of the theorems in this file state `True`: they compile, they carry `sorry`, and they say NOTHING. certo could not render those statements in Mathlib and will not guess at an encoding -- transcribe them from the comments above each one before this file is worth anything.
leancheck.empty_term: an empty term in a polynomial
leancheck.bad_factor: `{got}` is not a variable, an integer or a rational, and this parser refuses what it does not recognise rather than guessing
leancheck.not_zero: the relation is not against zero (`{got}`), which is the only form certo emits
leancheck.no_goal: no goal line of the form `: <poly> REL 0 := by`
leancheck.hollow: the statement is HOLLOW, so there is nothing to correspond to the certificate
leancheck.no_rows: a {kind} certificate carries no linear rows to compare against
cli.lean.corresponds: the exported statement CORRESPONDS to the certificate: {n} hypotheses and the goal, re-parsed from the file and compared
cli.lean.mismatch: the exported statement does NOT correspond to the certificate -- missing: {missing}; unexpected: {extra}; altered: {changed}; goal matches: {goal}
prop.not_bool: `{got}` has sort {sort}, not Bool. Encoding an arithmetic comparison as a boolean variable gives a CNF whose refutation says nothing about the arithmetic -- that is a wrong answer, not a missing feature. Mixed problems go to `prove`
prop.not_atom: `{got}` is not a propositional atom and not a connective this understands
prop.quantifier: quantifiers are not propositional logic; `prove` decides them and `cases` cannot
prop.means_valid: the formula is VALID: its negation was encoded, and the refutation of that negation is the proof
prop.means_sat: the formula is SATISFIABLE exactly when this CNF is, and a model restricted to the original variables is a model of the formula
cli.prop.auxiliaries: {atoms} variables of yours, {n} added by the encoding and dropped from the answer
